classification.classification_note: The saved MemorySanitizer report points to `if (rightNeighbor < owner)` in `cellToVertex`, so the witnessed bug is a branch use of an uninitialized stack `H3Index`, not a bounds error.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42515924 (h3): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzzerVertexes [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42515924
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/h3` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 16-byte witness `35 ff 20 20 20 20 ff 20 ff ff ff ff 20 20 20 20` is reinterpreted by `fuzzerVertexes` as `inputArgs { index = 0x20ff20202020ff35, vertexNum = -1 }`. The first harness call `cellToVertex(args->index, args->vertexNum, &out)` exits at `vertexNum < 0`, but the harness then unconditionally calls `cellToVertexes(args->index, outArr)`, whose loop invokes `cellToVertex()` again with in-range vertex numbers on the same invalid H3 cell. Inside `cellToVertex`, the witness index is treated as a resolution-15 non-pentagon cell and its digit sequence contains `INVALID_DIGIT` (`7`) at resolutions 11 and 12. On the crashing path the function enters owner selection, reaches the right-neighbor lookup `h3NeighborRotations(cell, right, &rRotations, &rightNeighbor)`, and that lookup returns `E_CELL_INVALID` before the success store `*out = current` because it encounters an invalid digit. The vulnerable caller ignores the `H3Error`, so stack variable `rightNeighbor` remains unwritten and the subsequent comparison `if (rightNeighbor < owner)` consumes it. MemorySanitizer reports that branch at `src/h3lib/lib/vertex.c:243:17` and attributes the uninitialized value to the `rightNeighbor` stack slot in `cellToVertex`. The fix captures the `h3NeighborRotations` return code, returns it before using `rightNeighbor`, and adds a regression test for the same H3 index.

source.description: First project statement inside the vulnerable function that consumes the witness H3 index and materializes the per-call state used by the later unchecked neighbor lookup.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 16-byte witness `35 ff 20 20 20 20 ff 20 ff ff ff ff 20 20 20 20`. The harness interprets it as `inputArgs`, so `args->index == 0x20ff20202020ff35` and `args->vertexNum == -1`; after the direct `cellToVertex(args->index, args->vertexNum, &out)` call exits at the `vertexNum < 0` guard, `cellToVertexes(args->index, outArr)` invokes this function again with in-range loop vertex numbers on the same invalid cell.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. `cellToVertex` branches on the uninitialized `rightNeighbor` value immediately after the unchecked right-neighbor lookup returns.
sink.note: The saved MSan trace reports `/src/h3/src/h3lib/lib/vertex.c:243:17` in `cellToVertex`, and no earlier use of `rightNeighbor` is reported.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `cellToVertex` performs the right-neighbor lookup but never captures or checks the returned `H3Error`, so an error path leaves the `rightNeighbor` out-parameter uninitialized and execution still falls through to the comparison at line 243.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this call to `H3Error rightNeighborError = h3NeighborRotations(...); if (rightNeighborError) return rightNeighborError;`, which is exactly the missing obligation in the vulnerable source.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete local stack slot named by the saved MemorySanitizer origin report. This output variable has no initializer before it is passed by address to the unchecked right-neighbor lookup.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: MemorySanitizer says the uninitialized value was created by stack allocation of `rightNeighbor` in the `cellToVertex` frame. The exact local declaration used on the crashing path is this line.
tainted_value_origin.note: If `h3NeighborRotations` reached its success store `*out = current` at `src/h3lib/lib/algos.c:475`, this stack slot would become defined. The later sink proves that did not happen on the witnessed path.

parser_admitted.description: After the size check, the harness always passes the witness `args->index` into `cellToVertexes`. For the staged witness, the preceding direct `cellToVertex(args->index, args->vertexNum, &out)` call uses `vertexNum == -1` and exits at line 210, so the saved MSan crash comes from this later `cellToVertexes` path.

evidence_limitations: The staged reproducer checkout is `f581626150e2e2b02f0ee1636084dfb8a4563abf`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit` `93308d2d1ab08fc275bbaa946693f868c07ee4f2`. This GT is grounded in the exact staged tree whose line map matches the saved MSan report.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not instrument the workspace. The exact internal `h3NeighborRotations` walk is therefore closed statically from the witness digit layout, the vulnerable source, the saved MSan origin/sink, and the staged fix's regression for the same H3 index.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the crashing `cellToVertexes` iteration, the witness H3 index `0x20ff20202020ff35` is decoded here into `cellIsPentagon == 0`, `cellNumVerts == 6`, and `res == 15`. Interpreting the same 64-bit value with H3's digit macros also shows `INVALID_DIGIT` (`7`) at resolutions 11 and 12, which later makes the right-neighbor traversal fail.

The owner-selection path executes. For the witness cell, `H3_GET_INDEX_DIGIT(cell, 15) == 5`, so the cell is not a center child and `cellToVertex` proceeds to consult neighboring cells instead of keeping `owner = cell`.

fine_trace.code:
h3NeighborRotations(cell, left, &lRotations, &leftNeighbor);
if (leftNeighbor < owner) owner = leftNeighbor;
fine_trace.note: Using `left = directionForVertexNum(cell, vertexNum)`, `cellToVertex` successfully materializes the left neighbor and updates the current owner candidate if needed. Because this call writes `leftNeighbor`, the later MSan origin cannot come from the left-neighbor slot.

The fast-path skip for the right neighbor is not taken. On the crashing path this predicate is true, so `cellToVertex` continues into the vulnerable right-neighbor lookup instead of stopping after the left-neighbor result.
MemorySanitizer origin. The right-neighbor out-parameter storage is allocated on the stack with no initializer before the guarded right-neighbor code runs.

Root-cause step. With `right = directionForVertexNum(cell, (vertexNum - 1 + cellNumVerts) % cellNumVerts)`, the function calls the right-neighbor traversal but does not store or test its `H3Error`. If that traversal fails, execution still falls through with `rightNeighbor` unchanged.

During the step-6 right-neighbor traversal, `h3NeighborRotations` encounters one of the witness cell's `INVALID_DIGIT` (`7`) digits and returns `E_CELL_INVALID` before reaching the success write `*out = current` at line 475. The out-parameter `rightNeighbor` therefore remains exactly as allocated in step 5.
Sink. After the step-7 error return, `cellToVertex` immediately compares the still-uninitialized `rightNeighbor` against `owner`. This branch is the first observed use that MemorySanitizer reports.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSan report attributes the origin to the `cellToVertex` stack frame at function entry; the concrete unwritten local on the crashing path is `H3Index rightNeighbor;` at line 240.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved MemorySanitizer trace reports `/src/h3/src/h3lib/lib/vertex.c:243:17` in `cellToVertex`, which is exactly the sink anchored above.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSan names the `rightNeighbor` stack allocation in `cellToVertex`, and the staged fix adds the missing return-value check immediately before that same variable is compared.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `cellToVertex -> cellToVertexes -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, matching the fine trace's right-neighbor failure in `cellToVertex` reached from the `cellToVertexes` loop.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 7 returns `E_CELL_INVALID` before writing the out-parameter, step 6 ignores that error, and step 8 is the first observed branch that consumes the still-uninitialized `rightNeighbor`.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch stores the right-neighbor lookup result in `rightNeighborError`, returns it immediately if non-zero, and adds a regression test that expects `E_CELL_INVALID` for the same witness index `0x20ff20202020ff35`.

format.name: fuzzerVertexes inputArgs struct
format.contract: The only verified trigger is the exact staged 16-byte `inputArgs` witness `35 ff 20 20 20 20 ff 20 ff ff ff ff 20 20 20 20`. In the staged harness this decodes to `index = 0x20ff20202020ff35`, `vertexNum = -1`, plus four trailing padding bytes. Source semantics show the crash is keyed by the first field: the direct `cellToVertex(args->index, args->vertexNum, &out)` call exits at the negative-`vertexNum` guard, while the later `cellToVertexes(args->index, outArr)` call ignores `vertexNum` and reaches the unchecked right-neighbor path for this exact invalid H3 index.
